name: ARN Smart Visitor Intent
author: arnsmart

sections.description:
ARN Smart Visitor Intent helps WordPress site owners understand why visitors came before the first conversation begins.

A lightweight sticky bar opens into an intent panel where visitors can select their reason for visiting and optionally share contact information. Built-in display rules and triggers control when the panel appears, while analytics reveal views, opens, responses, dismissals, contact activity, and intent distribution.

The plugin also includes privacy and consent tools, CSV export, email notifications, WordPress Mail and SMTP delivery options, plus a separate contact widget for Call, Email, and WhatsApp.

Visitor Intent Capture

  • Sticky bottom bar and expandable panel
  • Editable visitor intent choices
  • Optional contact form
  • Editable labels, placeholders, and messages
  • AJAX submission without page reload
  • Spam honeypot and nonce protection

Display Rules

  • Homepage or sitewide display
  • Include or exclude selected pages
  • Filter by public post type
  • Logged-in and logged-out visitors
  • Desktop and mobile visibility
  • First-time and returning visitors

Trigger System

  • Instant display
  • Delay by seconds
  • Scroll-depth trigger
  • Exit-intent trigger
  • Page-view trigger
  • Time-on-site trigger
  • Shortcode trigger
  • JavaScript API trigger

Analytics and Data

  • Views and panel opens
  • Response, dismissal, and contact rates
  • Intent distribution
  • Weekly and monthly statistics
  • Contact widget opens
  • Call, Email, and WhatsApp clicks
  • CSV export
  • Manual and automatic response cleanup
  • Manual and automatic display-cache reset

Privacy and Consent

  • Optional consent checkbox
  • Fully editable consent label and text
  • WordPress policy page selector
  • Modal, same-page, or new-tab policy opening
  • Optional required consent before submission
  • Only the acceptance status is stored

Notifications and SMTP

  • Email notifications
  • Optional notifications only when contact details are provided
  • WordPress Mail delivery
  • Existing SMTP plugin mode
  • Detection for common SMTP plugins
  • Internal SMTP configuration
  • SMTP connection test

Contact Widget

  • Separate floating contact widget
  • Call action
  • Email action
  • WhatsApp action
  • Editable title, description, and labels
  • Desktop and mobile visibility
  • Left or right positioning

Visitor and Website Intelligence

  • Visitor Intelligence: insights about visitor intent, contact behavior, trigger performance, pages, time periods, and conversion funnels
  • Website Intelligence: Google Analytics and Search Console data read from an installed and connected Google Site Kit plugin
  • 7, 30, and 90-day periods with current-versus-previous comparisons
  • Optional AI insights with your own API key from the provider you choose under Settings > ARN Free AI (off by default; see External services)
  • AI connection, token prices, monthly limits and usage history are managed on the shared Settings > ARN Free AI screen of ARN Free plugins
  • Built-in rule-based insights when AI is off or unavailable

Growth Intelligence

  • Data health for Google Analytics and Search Console through Site Kit: comparability, sample support, and data freshness
  • Comparison of completed, equal-length 7, 30, and 90-day periods ending yesterday
  • Accessible charts with exact daily values
  • Sustained traffic drop alerts and verified metric findings
  • Pages with declining search click-through rate, with a direct “Edit page” link
  • Largest page, channel, and device changes

Recommendations Block

  • “Visioix Recommendations” block and [arnvisiox_recommendations count="4"] shortcode
  • Shows your latest published posts by default
  • Optional, consent-based personalization: with the visitor’s consent, interest categories are kept only in the visitor’s browser for 30 days; no AI is used on the frontend
  • Global Privacy Control turns personalization off

External services

The plugin works without external services. Two optional features use them:

AI insights (ARN Free AI). This plugin does not contact any ARN server. AI features are off until a site administrator turns on AI Insights in Visitor Intent > Settings and sets up a provider under Settings > ARN Free AI.

When an administrator chooses a provider and enters their own API key, the plugin sends the text needed for the requested task to that provider only, at the moment the task runs. The API key is stored encrypted in the WordPress database. No data is sent to any other provider.

Requests are sent from your server only when:

  • a visitor response is saved while AI Insights is on: the response fields allowed in the AI privacy settings (by default the selected intent and the message; name, email, LinkedIn, and company only if you enable them), processed in the background;
  • an administrator generates AI Insights: aggregate visitor statistics (counts only);
  • an administrator generates the website diagnosis: Google Analytics and Search Console comparison figures read through Site Kit, such as metrics and the names of pages, queries, countries, devices, and channels;

  • an administrator clicks “Test connection” (a fixed test prompt, no site content) or “Load models” (the provider’s model list) under Settings > ARN Free AI.

  • OpenAI: https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use , https://openai.com/policies/privacy-policy

  • Anthropic (Claude): https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms , https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy
  • Google Gemini: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/terms , https://policies.google.com/privacy
  • DeepSeek: https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-terms-of-use.html , https://cdn.deepseek.com/policies/en-US/deepseek-privacy-policy.html
  • Moonshot AI (Kimi): https://platform.kimi.ai/docs/agreement/userprivacy
  • xAI (Grok): https://x.ai/legal/terms-of-service , https://x.ai/legal/privacy-policy
  • Mistral AI: https://legal.mistral.ai/terms , https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/privacy-policy
  • OpenAI-compatible endpoint: requests go to the address the administrator enters; that service’s own terms apply.

If WordPress AI is chosen instead, requests go through the provider connected in WordPress (Settings > Connectors) under that provider’s terms.

The bundled ARN Free AI module keeps its settings in the arn_free_ai_settings option and daily AI usage totals (no prompts, answers or keys) in the {prefix}arn_free_ai_usage database table.

Google Site Kit (Google Analytics and Search Console). Website Intelligence and Growth Intelligence do not contact Google themselves. They read reports from the Google Site Kit plugin through your site’s own REST API on the server; Site Kit connects to Google with your site’s own connection. See the Site Kit plugin and Google’s terms (https://policies.google.com/terms) and privacy policy (https://policies.google.com/privacy).

The recommendations block, the visitor panel, and the contact widget do not use external services.

Other ARN Smart Products

  • ARN Smart Visioix — professional visitor and website intelligence, forms, automations, experiments, reporting, and AI-guided action planning.
  • ARN Smart URL Manager — free short links, redirects, QR codes, URL health, bio pages, and local analytics.
  • ARN Smart Linkix — professional link operations with custom permalinks, canonical safety, smart routing, branded QR tools, and advanced analytics.
  • ARN Smart Site Utilities for Elementor — free Elementor components and site utilities.
  • ARN Smart Image Optimizer — lightweight image optimization and modern image delivery for WordPress.

Learn more at https://arnsmart.com
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/arn-smart-visitor-intent, or install the ZIP through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate ARN Smart Visitor Intent.
  3. Open Visitor Intent > Settings.
  4. Configure the intent panel, display rules, triggers, privacy, notifications, and contact widget.
  5. Review collected responses and analytics under the Visitor Intent admin menu.
sections.faq:
Is this a contact form plugin?

Not primarily. The plugin is designed to capture visitor intent first and optionally collect contact information afterward.

Can I display the panel only on selected pages?

Yes. You can use homepage, sitewide, include, exclude, and post-type display rules.

Can I control when the panel appears?

Yes. Instant, delay, scroll, exit intent, page views, time on site, shortcode, and JavaScript triggers are available.

Does it support GDPR or KVKK consent?

The plugin provides configurable consent and policy-display tools. Site owners remain responsible for configuring them according to their legal requirements.

Does it include WhatsApp?

Yes. The Contact Widget supports Call, Email, and WhatsApp actions without requiring another floating contact plugin.

Does internal SMTP replace my existing SMTP plugin?

No. You can continue using WordPress Mail or an existing SMTP plugin. Internal SMTP is optional.

Where are responses stored?

Responses are stored in WordPress and can be reviewed, exported as CSV, cleaned manually, or removed automatically according to your settings. Only administrators can view responses.

What do I need for Website and Growth Intelligence?

The Google Site Kit plugin, installed and connected to Google Analytics and Search Console. This plugin reads the data from Site Kit on your own site.

What does the recommendations block store?

Nothing until the visitor agrees. With consent, interest categories are stored in the visitor’s browser (localStorage) and a consent cookie (arnvisiox_growth_consent) is set for 30 days. Logged-in users see the general list. Global Privacy Control disables personalization.

Do I need to clear my page cache after updating?

Only when you update from a 2.0.x release: clear your page cache so visitors load the frontend script introduced in 2.1.0. Submissions from pages cached with the 2.0.x script are rejected until the page is refreshed. Updating from 2.1.0 or later does not change the frontend scripts.

My site is behind Cloudflare or another proxy. Which visitor address is used?

By default the direct connection (REMOTE_ADDR), which behind a proxy is the proxy’s address, so all visitors share one response limit. Under Visitor Intent > Settings > Limits & Proxy, choose “Behind a proxy or CDN”, the header your proxy sets, and the proxy’s IP addresses or CIDR ranges. The header is read only for requests that come from those addresses.

Where do I set the AI provider and API key?

Under Settings > ARN Free AI, the shared AI screen of ARN Free plugins: provider, your own API key, model, token prices, usage history and monthly limits. AI Insights itself and the AI privacy choices stay in Visitor Intent > Settings.

Do my AI settings move to ARN Smart Visioix (Pro)?

No. ARN Smart Visioix uses its own AI connection under Settings > ARN Center and does not read the ARN Free AI settings, so enter your AI provider API key there again after switching. The AI usage history recorded by this plugin stays under Settings > ARN Free AI and is not shown in the Pro Cost & Usage screen.

What is removed when I delete the plugin?

Sites where ARN Smart Visioix (Pro) is active are left untouched. On the other sites scheduled tasks are always removed, and responses, settings and analytics are kept unless “Delete all plugin data when the plugin is deleted” is on in the plugin settings; with it on, the plugin’s tables, options and transients are removed on each site where the option is on. The shared ARN Free AI settings, saved API keys and usage history of those sites are removed too, but only when no other installed ARN Free plugin (active or not) still uses them.
sections.changelog:
2.1.0

  • New: Growth Intelligence page with data health and completed-period comparison for Google Analytics and Search Console (via Site Kit): source health, accessible charts with data tables, sustained traffic drop alerts, verified findings, declining search CTR pages, and largest page, channel, and device changes.
  • New: Visioix Recommendations block and [arnvisiox_recommendations] shortcode with optional, consent-based personalization stored only in the visitor’s browser (30 days, no AI on the frontend).
  • New: AI features use the bundled ARN Free AI module and its Settings > ARN Free AI screen, shared by ARN Free plugins: choose OpenAI, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, DeepSeek, Kimi, xAI Grok, Mistral, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or WordPress AI (WordPress 7.0 or later); token prices, monthly limits and usage history in one place.
  • New: Settings > Limits & Proxy. The number of responses per visitor network every 10 minutes is adjustable (default 20).
  • New: daily limits for notification emails and AI analyses of responses (default 200 each). Responses are always saved; once a limit is reached, no more emails are sent or no more responses are analysed until the next day. Responses that were not analysed show the AI status “Skipped”.
  • New: visitor activity events are limited to 300 requests per visitor network every 10 minutes; further events are ignored without an error.
  • New: sites behind a proxy or CDN can read the visitor address from X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP, CF-Connecting-IP or True-Client-IP, only for requests from the trusted proxy addresses entered in the settings. The default remains the direct connection.
  • Changed: the provider, API key, model, endpoint and token price fields moved from Visitor Intent > Settings to Settings > ARN Free AI. Existing settings, the encrypted key and the AI usage history move automatically the first time an administrator opens a wp-admin page after the update; the old Visioix AI usage table is removed after the import is verified.
  • Changed: Visitor Intelligence > Cost & Usage and the AI usage summary read the usage recorded by ARN Free AI (imported history included); the website diagnosis is now counted too.
  • Changed: busy provider answers (HTTP 429 and 5xx) of the website diagnosis are retried automatically a limited number of times; background response analysis keeps its own queue retries.
  • Security: visitor responses are visible only to administrators; submissions use single-use tickets, size limits, and per-IP and per-session quotas; the visit reason must be one of the configured options.
  • Improved: visitor events are sent in batches and daily counters are stored atomically; events and counters are kept for two years.
  • Improved: spreadsheet-safe CSV export (PHP 8.4 compatible) and a PHP 8.4 deprecation fix.
  • Improved: upgrade and maintenance tasks no longer run on every dashboard request.
  • Improved: deactivation removes all scheduled tasks; uninstall always removes scheduled tasks, and with “delete data on uninstall” it removes all plugin tables, options, and transients on every site of a network; sites where ARN Smart Visioix is active are left untouched.
  • Fix: on sites that use the SQLite database, such as WordPress Playground and WordPress Studio, the abandonment section of Visitor Intelligence shows its numbers and close reasons instead of a database error. Sites on MySQL or MariaDB show the same results as before.
  • Removed: the Visioix “Test Connection” button; use “Test connection” under Settings > ARN Free AI.
  • Note: ARN Smart Visioix (Pro) uses its own AI connection; after switching to Pro, enter your AI provider API key there again.

2.0.3

  • Declared and reviewed compatibility with WordPress 7.1.
  • Batched large response exports and deletion operations to reduce memory pressure.
  • Preserved CSV formula-injection protection for visitor-controlled values.
  • Standardized product discovery links for the ARN Smart plugin family.

2.0.2

  • Removed legacy admin declarations now owned by the shared UI measurement system.
  • Removed duplicate CSS declarations and unused legacy admin component selectors without changing rendered styles.

2.0.1

  • Added the shared Visioix admin UI measurement system used by both Free and Pro.
  • Standardized page rhythm, cards, compact blocks, rows, headings, tabs, controls, tables, and responsive spacing.

2.0.0

  • Added Visitor Intelligence with data-driven insights for visitor intent, contact behavior, trigger performance, pages, time periods, and conversion funnels.
  • Added Website Intelligence integration through Google Site Kit, supporting Google Analytics and Search Console data.
  • Added 7, 30, and 90-day analysis periods with current-versus-previous period comparisons.
  • Added website performance monitoring for users, sessions, views, engagement rate, bounce rate, clicks, impressions, CTR, and average search position.
  • Added traffic change detection to identify increasing, decreasing, and stable website metrics.
  • Added Search Highlights for top queries, pages, countries, devices, and acquisition channels.
  • Added Product Highlights for fastest-growing, most-visited, highest-engagement, and highest-exit pages or products.
  • Added AI-powered Website Highlights with supporting evidence, confidence levels, and deterministic fallback analysis.
  • Added Response Intelligence for response summaries, topic detection, priority assessment, follow-up recommendations, and response status.
  • Added visitor analysis dashboards for overview, summary, trends, segments, intent, contact behavior, triggers, time analysis, and funnel performance.
  • Added AI Heatmaps for intent, contact, trigger performance, and funnel drop-off analysis.
  • Added period-based insight snapshots and historical analysis records.
  • Added duplicate snapshot prevention and analysis engine version tracking.
  • Added AI Queue management with retry support and new-data detection.
  • Added Cost & Usage reporting for input tokens, output tokens, provider usage, model usage, daily consumption, monthly consumption, and estimated AI costs.
  • Added configurable AI providers and models using the website owner’s own API credentials.
  • Added AI privacy controls for managing which visitor and website data may be included in AI requests.
  • Added confidence controls and limited-data warnings to prevent strong conclusions from insufficient data.
  • Added clear identification of AI-generated and Visioix Engine-generated insights.
  • Added deterministic fallback processing for unavailable providers, timeouts, malformed responses, and invalid AI output.
  • Added Privacy & Consent controls with editable labels, consent text, policy-page selection, opening method, and required-consent enforcement.
  • Added consent status to response records and CSV exports.
  • Added SMTP configuration with test-email support, delivery logging, external SMTP detection, and WordPress mail compatibility.
  • Added configurable contact actions for phone, email, and WhatsApp.
  • Added a floating WhatsApp contact option.
  • Added display rules for homepage, sitewide, selected pages, excluded pages, post types, visitor login state, device type, and visit status.
  • Added advanced display triggers including delay, scroll depth, exit intent, page views, time on site, shortcode, and JavaScript activation.
  • Added automatic and manual data-cleanup controls.
  • Added expanded CSV export support for visitor responses, intelligence data, consent records, and analytics fields.
  • Improved the administration interface with reorganized Visitor Analytics and Visitor Intelligence sections.
  • Improved analytics navigation, period selection, dashboard cards, status indicators, evidence presentation, and responsive administration layouts.
  • Improved Google Site Kit connection handling and invalid-report recovery.
  • Improved compatibility with Elementor and other WordPress administration styles.
  • Improved data validation, sanitization, escaping, capability checks, nonce verification, and error handling across administration and submission workflows.
  • Improved AI credential handling with encrypted storage, masked fields, protected updates, and automatic migration of previously stored credentials.
  • Improved SMTP credential security with authenticated AES-256-GCM encryption and automatic migration of existing passwords.
  • Prevented API keys and SMTP passwords from being exposed in administration-page HTML.
  • Prevented credentials from being stored as plain text when secure encryption is unavailable.
  • Added CSV formula-injection protection for visitor-controlled export values.
  • Fixed response metadata being processed before a valid response record was created.
  • Fixed missing metadata backfill markers on newly submitted responses.
  • Fixed an undefined diagnosis variable in deterministic Website Intelligence results.
  • Fixed evidence summaries not being included in fallback diagnosis output.
  • Replaced an unused phone-data AI permission with a LinkedIn-data permission matching the available response fields.
  • Removed unused administration callbacks, redundant header parameters, and unnecessary action calculations.
  • Removed obsolete and unreachable code while preserving WordPress hooks, dynamic callbacks, and extension points.
  • Improved overall codebase stability, maintainability, packaging integrity, and upgrade compatibility.

1.0.0

  • First stable release.
  • Added visitor intent capture and optional contact fields.
  • Added display rules for pages, post types, devices, login state, and visitor type.
  • Added instant, delay, scroll, exit-intent, page-view, time-on-site, shortcode, and JavaScript triggers.
  • Added analytics, intent distribution, weekly and monthly statistics, and CSV export.
  • Added response retention, cleanup, and display-cache controls.
  • Added privacy consent, policy page selection, and required-consent validation.
  • Added WordPress Mail, external SMTP plugin, and internal SMTP delivery methods.
  • Added SMTP testing and common SMTP plugin detection.
  • Added floating Contact Widget with Call, Email, and WhatsApp actions.
  • Added contact-action analytics.
